blindSourceSummaries: Court record: the landmark ruling for a trans inmate against the corrections department, in an equality sitting of a local division of the high court (judgment 10 November 2025): refusal of gender expression (feminine attire, she/her pronouns), inadequate accommodation and denial of state-funded gender-affirming hormone therapy were held to be unfair discrimination; hormone therapy was recognised as part of the constitutional right to adequate medical treatment.

A public-interest law centre's case page (14 November 2025): summary of the high-court ruling for a transgender inmate against the corrections department - unfair discrimination and harassment by refusing feminine clothing, correct pronouns and appropriate accommodation; the court held gender-affirming hormonal therapy must be provided at state expense and ordered the department to implement its own procedures for transgender inmates immediately.

A national human-rights body's media statement (14 November 2025): welcomes the 10 November 2025 high-court ruling for a transgender inmate; describes its monitoring mandate over places of detention and the inmate's account (initially allowed to express her gender, later restricted from feminine clothing and make-up, misgendered, denied prescribed hormone therapy), and the court's finding that gender-affirming healthcare forms part of adequate medical treatment.
blindOutOfScope: General violent-crime and gender-based-violence rates in this state/province are elevated; this is ordinary-crime context and does not move trans-specific risk (the reporting identifies no trans victims).
